thread:
jia: uploaded an nsys capture from the 4k-batch tail-latency regression. trace: perfetto://redwood/trace/2534123456

jia: TL;DR: top time consumers are surprising — `attn_kv_fetch` and `batch_pack_memcpy` dominate >60% of GPU time, not the expected `attn_compute` kernel. attaching the sample table below.

sam: can you paste the nsys summary table? also which model/config (seq len / head / fp)?

jia: model: rw-7b-v2, seq=2048, batch=4096 -> effective tokens high. fp16, cuda 12.2

jia: ```
GPU Kernel Summary (nsys):
1) attn_kv_fetch         34.2%  (30.1 ms)
2) batch_pack_memcpy     28.7%  (25.3 ms)  <-- suspicious host->device pattern
3) attn_compute         15.6%  (13.7 ms)
4) kv_cache_apply        8.4%   (7.4 ms)
5) softmax               3.1%   (2.7 ms)
other                   10.0%  (8.6 ms)
```

alex: interesting — `attn_kv_fetch` sounds like our kernel that assembles interleaved KV reads. Could be warp divergence + uncoalesced loads. `batch_pack_memcpy` being that high suggests repeated memcpy during batching step (maybe our batching path is re-copying prefixes per shard).

marcos: did the trace show PCIe memcpy streams? perfetto has the DMA timeline. perf-bot, did you capture memcpy timelines?

perf-bot: perfetto link: https://perfetto.dev/trace/2534123456
perf-bot: memcpy activity: high-frequency host->device bursts aligning with user request bursts at ~30ms intervals.

sam: hypothesis: our batching heuristic is re-packing inputs per shard for every micro-batch instead of reusing KV-prefetch buffer. That explains memcpy spike. Also attn_kv_fetch may be doing per-request bounds-check branching leading to SM underutilization.

alex: propose quick repro: run with env `REDWOOD_BATCH_REUSE=1` to force reuse of packing buffer and `REDWOOD_KERNEL_HINT=coalesced-kv` to prefer the coalesced KV kernel. If memcpy drops and attn_kv_fetch time drops -> good.

jia: I can run that. Also will capture `nsys --sample=stack` to get kernel-level PC stacks for attn_kv_fetch to see branch hotspots.

marcos: rank priorities: (1) avoid hot memcpy (2) address attn_kv_fetch divergence (3) consider fallback kernel if SM occupancy low.

sam: small experiment idea: reduce batch from 4096->2048 to see whether memcpy scales linearly. If so, it's batching policy bug.

jia: running quick tests now, will post results. thanks all :thumbsup:

(10m later)

jia: results: with REDWOOD_BATCH_REUSE=1 memcpy down from 25.3ms -> 6.2ms, attn_kv_fetch 30.1ms -> 18.4ms. overall tail P99 dropped ~22%.

alex: nice! that points squarely to packing reuse. next: we still have attn_kv_fetch at 18ms, need to look at its occupancy. can you attach `nvprof --metrics inst_executed,sm_efficiency` output?

jia: pasted quick nvprof snippet: ```
attn_kv_fetch: inst_executed=1.2e9, sm_efficiency=46%
attn_compute: inst_executed=2.8e9, sm_efficiency=78%
```

marcos: sm_efficiency 46% is a suspect — likely memory-bound or diverging. If coalesced-kv hint lowers insts and raises sm_eff -> okay. Also consider launching a smaller threadblock config kernel via kernel selector map for seq>1024.

sam: for rollout: create a canary config that enables `REDWOOD_BATCH_REUSE` by default and `REDWOOD_KERNEL_HINT=coalesced-kv` for the 7b family on Dedicated. Add a perf regression monitor check on P99 latency and token cost.

jia: created PR with quick flag + perf test. PR link: https://git.redwood/infer/PR/7821

alex: :rocket: we'll schedule a perfetto/nvsys follow-up to validate across regions. thanks team.

marcos: filing a short postmortem note in #incidents if the 4k batch customers saw regressions, add mitigation steps (flag + rollback).

sam: cool. closing thread once PR merged.
